speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Over the last decade, IRAS has also taken on the complementary function of disbursing broad-based grants to businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These refer to grants where Government administrative data is used to determine firm eligibility and grant quantum, and payouts are automatically disbursed without a need for businesses to apply.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Examples of such broad-based grants include the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and the Uplifting Employment Credit, which encourage firms to adopt progressive hiring practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, IRAS also played a pivotal role disbursing the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), the Rental Support Scheme and the Small Business Recovery Grant to support our businesses to tide over the challenging economic conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: At the height of COVID-19 in 2020, IRAS disbursed six-times that amount to more than 150,000 businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It will grant IRAS new powers to investigate fraud and abuse and also to seek recovery of monies when there are erroneous disbursements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The first key amendment grants IRAS the function of administering scheduled public schemes for and on behalf of the Government or any other statutory body.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In the past, the power to disburse grants was granted to IRAS through subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As disbursing grants becomes a larger part of IRAS' mandate, it is appropriate to include it as a key function in the IRAS Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The second key amendment enables IRAS to effectively audit and investigate cases of fraud and abuse of enterprise grants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: With the increase in the number of grants disbursed, there has been a corresponding rise in the number of fraud cases.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For instance, in 2022, the director and operations manager of a spa were convicted in Court for attempting to cheat IRAS into disbursing a JSS payout of approximately $50,000 during the pandemic in 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The duo had submitted false declarations and fake employment contracts for 28 individuals who did not perform work or receive salaries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Thanks to the vigilance of our IRAS colleagues, no disbursement was made as inconsistencies were detected in the documents provided.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As IRAS continues to enhance its capabilities to detect fraud, it currently lacks the legislative levers to investigate fraud and abuse pertaining to grants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Such cases have to be referred to the Police for investigation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These enforcement powers are similar to existing powers under the Income Tax and GST Acts, where IRAS investigators are empowered to investigate tax offences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We will also make it an offence to interfere with or refuse to comply with IRAS' investigation of serious grant offences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Those who are found guilty of the offence will be liable to a fine not exceeding $10,000 and/or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The amendments also set out the specific offences and punishments for obtaining or assisting another person to obtain a grant under the scheduled public schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Depending on the severity of the offence, those convicted will be liable to a penalty equal to one, two or three times the amount of payout overpaid or would have been overpaid; and a monetary fine and/or imprisonment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These penalties are aligned with the penalties for similar offences under the Income Tax and GST Acts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These debts owed to the Government could arise from either fraud or abuse, or further data updates or data errors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: So, as I have shared earlier, most of the grants are disbursed automatically by IRAS, where Government administrative data is used to determine firm eligibility and grant quantum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This allows disbursements to be made promptly and businesses, especially our small and medium enterprises (SMEs), do not need to expend additional effort to make applications.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, there could be errors discovered or further updates to the data after the monies have been disbursed, for instance, when a firm makes a genuine retrospective adjustment to its CPF contributions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As the eligibility assessment and grant quantum were computed based on outdated data, certain recipients might already have received more grants than they are entitled to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: When this happens, we propose that IRAS should have the power to recover the excess amounts from these recipients.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As these are public funds, even if the error was no fault of the recipients, they have a responsibility to return the overpaid amounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This can be done without penalties for recipients who are cooperative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The proposed legal powers, including the imposition of interest for late repayment, signal the serious nature of the issue and encourage firms to return any overpaid monies in a timely manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The remaining amendments to the Bill are operational and administrative in nature.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: They are to protect the identity of informers; allow IRAS to compound offences; allow service of documents by personal delivery or ordinary post; and allow a person to provide the documents and information required by IRAS for the investigation of an arrestable offence via electronic service.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three sets of clarifications to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on the recovery of wrongly given grant monies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill introduces offences for obtaining grants or assisting another person to obtain grants by giving false or misleading information.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister clarify that if multiple individuals are prosecuted in relation to a single grant, is it possible for IRAS to impose penalties on each offender?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In other words, even though only a single grant is or would have been wrongly disbursed, is IRAS entitled to recover a penalty from each and every individual prosecuted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification is on the new offences for providing false or misleading information.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Different offences are set out under section 17F(1), section 17F(3) and section 17F(5) depending on the state of the mind of the offender, for instance, whether the offending is carried out negligently or willfully with intent to obtain the grant.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The penalties and punishment that can be imposed is of varying severity depending on the section the prosecution is brought under.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To provide guidance on how prosecutorial discretion will be exercised, can Minister provide illustrations on when the different provisions will apply?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, on the new investigation and enforcement powers given to IRAS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With the new powers, can I check what steps will be taken to ensure that IRAS is prepared for the extended scope of powers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, Sir, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: IRAS has been an efficient tax authority and has a consistently low cost of tax collection at less than one cent per dollar of tax collected over the past decade or so.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In my speech today, I will first touch on the broader picture in IRAS' role surrounding the administration of grants, before following up on specific provisions of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: IRAS today is already responsible for administering enterprise disbursement schemes and is, in fact, also designated as the Centre of Excellence for disbursing broad-based grants to enterprises.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: These include the administration of enterprise schemes, such as the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, Senior Employment Credit and CPF Transition Offset.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: During COVID-19, IRAS also supported the administration of the Jobs Support Scheme, Jobs Growth Incentive, Rental Cash Grant and the Rental Support Scheme.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As described in the explanatory statement of the Bill, the amendments aim to provide for the recovery of any money, credit, rebate or other grant under schemes introduced by the Government or a statutory body that are specified in the new Second Schedule of the Act from recipients that are not entitled to such monies.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: To me, this begs the broader question, that had such recipients not cooperated with the Government in the past, were they legally entitled to retain these grants, given that these were given to them not as a result of deceit or fraud on the part of the recipients, but some form of administrative oversight or mistake on the part of the authorities?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: There was the recent case of overpayments in the Jobs Support Scheme, where the wage support grants were erroneously paid to about 5,400 companies in October 2020 due to mistakes in computing the disbursements.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The issue of overpayments was also an area that was highlighted in the thematic audit by the Auditor-General in its latest report, which looked at key COVID-19 grant schemes, the Jobs Support Scheme, the Rental Cash Grant and the Rental Support Scheme.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This issue was also part of the discussions by the Public Accounts Committee which I am a member of.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In any case, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) had updated the Committee that MOF and IRAS have taken steps to investigate and recover the overpayments, which made up less than 0.5% of total payouts across three schemes.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Overpayments in relation to Government-funded entities were fully recovered.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: On the other hand, in cases of abuse of such Government grant schemes or grants which were fraudulently obtained, it is important that IRAS be empowered with investigative and enforcement powers to deal with such offences to safeguard public monies.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Following the various reviews conducted by IRAS and the MOF in recent years and after internal processes highlighted in the Auditor-General's report are refined, does the Minister have further information to update on the cases of abuse uncovered and the monies subsequently recovered?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Moving on to specific provisions of the Bill, section 17D of the proposed Bill provides for IRAS to charge interest on the overpayments that it seeks to recover from recipients.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Given the overpayments were not the fault of recipients, what is IRAS' approach in the recovery process and how much leeway do companies have before interest in being levied on them?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Moreover, given that interest is to be calculated on a daily basis, from the end of the payment period to the date the claim amount is paid in full, this could rack up to a substantial interest charge.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: What are the indicative interest rates under consideration, how much interest was charged for COVID-19 grant recoveries and whether such interest payments can be waived should there be a good faith attempt to make the repayments?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This is especially considering section 17C, where a payment period of 30 days is proposed after the date of service of a written notice to the recipient is served.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While the Bill did state that "there can be a later time that the Authority may allow in a particular case", the tight timelines can be particularly onerous on companies which may be facing severe cash flow difficulties or SMEs which may not have as established administrative and finance processes in place, particularly if the amounts in question may be quite substantial relative to the recipient's financial position.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: All that being said, notwithstanding my clarifications, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, I have a few points of clarification.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will these two schemes and other schemes not listed be included in the Bill too?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The reason I ask is because I have met elderly and unemployed residents who have approached me for assistance as they have been requested to return the SIRS that they have received previously.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some shared that they did not apply personally for the grant and were assisted by their family members or friends.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, they cannot recall details of their application.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They also mentioned that they have already spent the SIRS money and do not have any money to pay back and are not working.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Does the Ministry have any indication if there was an increased amount of false claims during this period and hence, this Bill allows the smoother recovery from false or wrongly given claims?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How will the amendments in this Bill enhance the enforcement and prevent the fraudulent claims and provide more effectiveness to recover money that were disbursed based on false information?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A quick check on SkillsFuture website also shows that there are over 29,000 courses available.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Most courses have multiple vendors or course providers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, the course fees and hence, SkillsFuture grant varies.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Take Lean Sigma Green Belt Certification as an example.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The course leads to an industry accepted certification but one provider charges five times more per course and gets three times more the funding received by the other provider, for the same outcome for the participant.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am not referring to this specific example.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But how do we ensure course fees are not inflated and do not become an opportunity for companies to claim higher subsidies?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If there are excessive checks, will this deter those who truly are in need from seeking the support that they require?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Schemes like COVID Support Grant and SIRS supported those who lost their jobs or had a pay reduction during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Jobs Support Scheme made sure workers remain employed during challenging times.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I, for one, as one of the over 25,000 aerospace workers in the industry, saw first-hand how the Jobs Support Scheme managed to keep many Singaporeans employed when our borders were shut; the Small Business Recovery Grant assisted SMEs to stay afloat; SkillsFuture provided support for our workforce to upskill and upgrade to meet the needs of the future economy; and the Senior Employment Credit ensured seniors get an opportunity for employment.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, before I end my speech, I would just like to say a huge "thank you" to the Minister and all those working in the Ministries for working very hard to design and administer the grants and schemes for everyone who needs it, especially during the last few years.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Clarification notwithstanding, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Through support schemes such as those for the self-employed and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) owners, livelihoods were sustained and as a result, Singapore averted a serious economic crisis.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The initial roll-out was broad-based to avoid a deeper economic crisis, preserve jobs and maintain key corporate capabilities.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Speed was crucial to prevent interruption of cashflow for businesses and incomes for workers.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Civil servants from Statutory Boards like IRAS, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and Enterprise Singapore worked long hours for a long period of time so that assistance was rendered to the deserving applicants during the COVID-19 period.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These civil servants received many calls and chasers to approve and disburse the assistance.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, when they were flagged for overpayments due to calculation errors committed under time pressure, the remarks were not kind towards them.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Neither did I observe many beneficiaries who stood up for these civil servants.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, I would like to seek clarifications on the following.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Can IRAS also administer schemes like the Enterprise Sustainability Programme and Enterprise Financing Scheme?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will the proposed administrative amendments enhance the efficacy of whole-of-Government's grant administration?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The information submitted by the SMEs when they apply for other schemes can be relevant to the schemes which are managed by Enterprise Singapore currently.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that the Government cannot give subsidies to SMEs in an unabated manner, but SMEs will appreciate that the application processes of various schemes be synergised and simplified.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Time saved is as good as revenue earned.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What recourse does a business have if they disagree with IRAS' assessment that funds have been wrongly disbursed to them?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can they raise it to an independent assessment panel?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Bill also empowers IRAS officers to perform the investigative, audit and enforcement actions.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Officers can even arrest without warrant for arrestable offences and perform body searches.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will IRAS ensure that the investigative powers granted under this Bill will be used appropriately and in the public interest? : How much additional resources will be given to IRAS for the additional caseload as it will include investigation of fraud and abuse as well as recovery of wrongful disbursement?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does IRAS require additional budget to develop capabilities in-house to investigate and enforce penalties against cases of scheme abuse?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does IRAS plan to develop these in-house capabilities?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can they tap on Commercial Affairs Department for a start so as to minimise additional expenditure?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The amendments mention protecting the identity of informants.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does the legislation ensure this protection, and what penalties are in place for any breaches?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does allowing IRAS to compound offenses contribute to greater flexibility in dealing with grant non-compliances or scheme abuses that do not meet the threshold of criminal prosecution?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These refer to grants where Government administrative data is used to determine firm eligibility and grant quantum, and the payouts are disbursed without a need for the businesses to apply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, the examples that Mr Sharael Taha mentioned – SIRS, COVID Relief Grant – these were not administered by IRAS.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SIRS was administered by the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the COVID Relief Grant was administered by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS is able to play this role well as it has built up the IT systems and data linkages, payment mechanisms, and audit and fraud detection capabilities over the past decade.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Hence, other Government agencies can tap on IRAS' capabilities for such broad-based enterprise disbursements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Don Wee asked if IRAS can disburse application-based grants for businesses.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Unlike broad-based grants which are disbursed automatically based on pre-determined criteria, application-based grants require officers to assess the merit of each application in accordance with the intent of the grant.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Administering such application-based grants require specific industry or domain expertise which reside in Government agencies overseeing the respective industry sectors, and not with IRAS.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Entities that administer schemes for businesses do tap on data from other agencies including IRAS, to streamline the application process for enterprises and their processing of the grants.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The new Second Schedule lists the enterprise schemes which IRAS is administering, including schemes that it is winding down the disbursements and audits for.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Minister for Finance will update the Second Schedule as and when necessary to include new schemes for which IRAS' enterprise disbursement functions can serve.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS currently refers serious cases of fraud and scheme abuse to the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) under the Singapore Police Force.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, CAD only investigates fraud cases that are criminal in nature and offences under the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Before referring to CAD, IRAS would conduct its own investigation whenever there are cases of suspected abuse or fraud.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS currently does this by triangulating data and intelligence from various sources and looking for inconsistencies in submitted documentation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, IRAS does not have the legal powers at the moment to compel the provision of information or to conduct on-site inspections and checks.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This limits the reach and effectiveness of their investigation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is why we are tabling this Bill in this House.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As the volume and total value of grants disbursed by IRAS increases, IRAS will need to have the necessary powers to conduct investigations more effectively, recover public funds and safeguard public interest.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These powers are no different from what IRAS does for taxes today.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Likewise, there will be similar safeguards in place, where the investigative powers will be restricted to trained officers authorised by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS has developed its IT and data systems, disbursement mechanisms and fraud detection capabilities over the years.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will provide IRAS with sufficient resources to take on the enterprise disbursement role.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Louis Chua asked for updates on the fraud and abuse cases involving COVID-19 grants and the amount of money recovered so far.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Thus far, investigations into four cases that involve Jobs Support Scheme payouts, amounting to approximately $120,000 had concluded.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Three cases were successfully charged and convicted in Court, while one case was given a conditional warning.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: None of the $120,000 was disbursed as IRAS had detected the fraud early.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The remaining 21 cases reported by IRAS are currently being investigated by CAD.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As for wrongly paid grants, these are a small minority of the total amount of grants disbursed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And in response to Member's question, we did not charge interest.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With the amendments in this Bill, the process of recovering wrongly paid grants will remain largely unchanged and it is not expected to impact the large majority of grant recipients.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The amendments address the minority of cases – I would say the small minority of cases – allowing IRAS to impose interest only if the outstanding amount is not paid within the prescribed repayment period, which is usually within 30 days.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is to encourage timely repayment of public funds.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If the repayment is made within the prescribed period, there is no interest imposed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For late repayments, the interest rate will be based on the Government interest rate on instalment payments, with a spread of three percentage points.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: A business which disagrees with IRAS' assessment of wrongful disbursement can appeal to IRAS with relevant information to substantiate its case.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If the appeal is rejected and the recipient does not want to return the overpayment, IRAS may pursue legal action through the Courts – and then, it is for the Courts to decide the outcome.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The wrongly disbursed funds are public monies from our taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The overpayment may not be due to the fault of the recipients, but as I explained in my main speech, it is fair that they should return the overpaid amounts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If they face genuine difficulties and need more time to make the repayment, they can appeal to IRAS and we will assess each case individually.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are introduced to deter and penalise errant entities or persons for committing fraud and abuse.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS does not have any legal powers to take action against errant employers for scheme abusers today.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS can only refer cases to CAD, as I explained earlier, to investigate and prosecute under the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a deterrent against scheme abuse, IRAS will need powers to impose penalties for offences alongside its investigative powers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These limits are determined with reference to the penalties for similar offences in the Income Tax and Goods and Services Tax (GST) Acts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Although the maximum penalties may be lower than existing offences under the Penal Code, they are tailored to target and deter the specific misconduct associated with the payout schemes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IRAS will regularly review the effectiveness of these penalties.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The amendments will also grant IRAS the authority to compound offences, so, IRAS can offer composition as an alternative to prosecution.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This allows minor infractions to be dealt with quickly and efficiently.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Ng asked whether it is possible for IRAS to impose penalties on each offender if multiple individuals are prosecuted in relation to a single grant.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, two individuals, each one can be liable, separately, and individually.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These offences are meant to penalise those who had deliberately or assisted another person to provide false or misleading information with the intent to induce IRAS to provide a higher amount of payout.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With those clarifications, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do Members have any clarifications to seek from Minister?
